claims.text: In csv.DictReader, if a row has more fields than fieldnames, the remaining data is put in a list and stored with the fieldname specified by restkey (which defaults to None). If a non-blank row has fewer fields than fieldnames, the missing values are filled-in with the value of restval (which defaults to None).

claims.text: Under default csv.writer behavior, the value None is written as the empty string, so the output does not distinguish None from an empty string; this is not a reversible transformation.

citations.excerpt: the value None is written as the empty string. While this isn’t a reversible transformation, it makes it easier to dump SQL NULL data values to CSV files without preprocessing the data returned from a cursor.fetch* call.

claims.text: The default quoting for csv.writer is QUOTE_MINIMAL.

citations.excerpt: Controls when quotes should be generated by the writer and recognised by the reader. It can take on any of the QUOTE_* constants and defaults to QUOTE_MINIMAL.
